title: New User SOP
text:
Revision 1.0 [Spring 2026] 1 
Ingram Hall Makerspace – New Users 
First Steps 
1. Navigate to https://www.engineering.txst.edu/makerspace/documents.html 
a. Read the Ingram Hall Makerspace Policies and Procedures 
2. Next, navigate to https://www.engineering.txst.edu/makerspace/forms.html 
a. Complete and sign the Ingram Hall Makerspace Participation Agreement 
3. Both the Photograph Release and Indemnity and the Release of Liability, 
Indemnification and Assumption of the Risk Agreement (Adults & Minors) are 
available on the same webpage. To use the Makerspace for walk-in access, 
student organization activities, or personal projects, please complete and sign 
these forms, then proceed to FOM Account Creation (Page 2). 
a. The Photograph Release and Indemnity only needs to be completed once 
in your lifetime 
b. The Release of Liability, Indemnification and Assumption of the Risk 
Agreement needs to be completed once every academic year and expires 
annually on August 31st if over the age of 18. 
i. A different release is required for minors under the age of 18 and 
will expire on the signee’s 18th birthday. At which point, the annual 
form will need to be completed. 
c. All release form links are also found at 
https://www.engineering.txst.edu/makerspace/forms.html 
d. Use your TXST NetID as your email address. You will need to verify 
your email for all completed forms. 
4. If you decline to complete either release form, you are finished with new user 
onboarding. Your instructor or PI will handle all equipment reservations on your 
behalf.

text:

Ingram Hall Makerspace 
Account Creation for Research Usage 
For researchers wishing to use Makerspace resources, please follow the instructions 
below. Please allow at least 2 business days for processing of all forms and 
submissions. 
All agreement forms can be found at: engineering.txstate.edu/makerspace/forms.html 
1. Complete the Research Usage Request. 
2. Visit https://fom.engineering.txstate.edu 
3. After logging into FOM with your SSO credentials, you should be designated as a 
supervisor and see “supervisor home” on the left-hand menu. Navigate to this 
page to edit your research project members. 
a. Note that you may see a “missing financial account warning”, that will be 
removed after your form is processed. 
b. If your supervisor role is not active in FOM within three business days 
after all parties have completed the Research Usage Request form, 
please contact IHM to resolve the issue.

For instructors wishing to use Makerspace resources for course content, please follow

title: Ingram Hall Makerspace Policies and Procedures
file: Ingram Hall Makerspace Policies and Procedures.pdf
text:
Updated: February 2026 
Page 1 of 6 
Ingram Hall Makerspace Safety Rules and Procedures 
1. General Rules 
• Access is limited to TXST students, staff, faculty, or authorized guests. 
Unauthorized visitors are not allowed into any room of the Makerspace. 
• All users must complete and sign the Ingram Hall Makerspace Participation 
Agreement before entry to the facility is permitted. 
• Users must check-in when entering the Makerspace. A TXST ID card is required 
for entry. 
• Doors should never be opened for anyone. Doors must never be propped open 
unless explicitly authorized by Makerspace management. 
• Unlimited check-ins may occur daily during operating hours, checking out is not 
required. 
• Access to the Makerspace via adjacent rooms is strictly prohibited. All entry must 
occur through the front doors of PawPrint Studio (1st floor lobby entrance). 
• Users are responsible for managing their personal items, such as raw materials 
and data on makerspace computers. 
• Users are responsible for all samples, components, parts, assemblies, and raw 
materials stored in the facility. Items left outside designated storage areas will be 
considered abandoned and may be discarded. 
• Food and drinks are prohibited in all tool and machine areas, including anywhere 
in the Industrial area. Food and drinks are allowed in PawPrint Studio , 
provided they are not near equipment and the user cleans up after themselves. 
• Running, horseplay, or disruptive behavior is strictly prohibited. 
• All use of equipment and the facility as a whole is administered through the 
online management system, Facility Online Manager (FOM). FOM is reachable 
on and off campus at https://fom.engineering.txstate.edu/. 
• Please acknowledge the Ingram Hall Makerspace in all publications and grant 
applications where equipment use, services, and/or expertise provided by our 
staff contributed to the final work product. 
2. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) 
• PawPrint Studio has no PPE requirements. 
• Safety glasses, long pants, sleeved shirts, and closed-toe shoes must be worn at 
all times when in the Industrial Area. Sandals, slip-ons, flip-flops, or open-toe 
footwear are not allowed. Shirts may not expose shoulders or mid-section. 
• The same PPE requirements apply when passing through the industrial area to 
access adjacent rooms. 
• Long hair, loose clothing, and jewelry must be tied back or removed before 
operating equipment. 
• Users are responsible for providing their own safety glasses and dressing 
appropriately. Users will be denied access if attire is not appropriate.

title: Ingram Hall Makerspace Policies and Procedures
file: Ingram Hall Makerspace Policies and Procedures.pdf
text:
Updated: February 2026 
Page 2 of 6 
3. Equipment Usage 
• Users must sign up for equipment use under the correct project and account 
information. 
• Users may only operate equipment they have been trained and authorized to 
use. 
• Users must adhere to Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and policy when 
utilizing equipment. Failure to adhere to SOP/policy is considered intentional or 
negligent equipment misuse. 
• In-person training expires if equipment is not used within 180 days of the last 
use. Each use resets the 180-day period. 
• Online policy and procedure quizzes must be renewed every 150 days, 
regardless of equipment or facility usage. These serve as a refresher and ensure 
awareness of updated policies and procedures. 
• Some equipment and rooms may require completion of an external learning 
course as part of the training process. One example is LinkedIn Learning, which 
requires a LinkedIn account and profile. LinkedIn Learning is available to all 
Faculty, Staff, Students at no additional cost. Click here to visit ITAC webpage for 
more info. Once completed, these certificates do not expire for equipment 
training purposes. 
• Equipment must be inspected prior to use. Do not operate tools that are 
damaged or malfunctioning. Report any broken or unsafe equipment to staff 
immediately. This may be done either by email or through FOM. 
• In case of equipment malfunction during operation, stop use immediately and 
notify staff. 
• Never leave equipment running unattended. 3D Printers are the only equipment 
that does not require you to be present during the full duration of the print. 
• Do not attempt to bypass safety guards. 
• Do not modify equipment or deviate from SOPs without staff approval. 
• No weapons, or anything resembling a weapon, may be fabricated within the 
facility. 
• After use, check-in equipment in FOM, power off equipment, clean the area, and 
return tools to their designated locations. 
4. Workspace Procedures 
• Keep aisles, exits, and emergency equipment clear at all times. Backpacks 
should be place under desks or on hangers. 
• Hazardous materials (e.g., solvents, adhesives, chemicals) must be labeled and 
used only in designated areas with approval. 
• All spills must be cleaned immediately. 
• Waste materials must be disposed of in the proper containers (scrap bins, 
chemical disposal, etc.).

title: Ingram Hall Makerspace Policies and Procedures
file: Ingram Hall Makerspace Policies and Procedures.pdf
text:
Updated: February 2026 
Page 3 of 6 
• Project and work tables, including those in IGRM 1202D, are not to be used for 
storage and must remain clear when not in active use. Items left on tables may 
be moved or discarded as necessary, and the facility is not responsible for loss 
or damage resulting from such actions. 
5. Emergency Procedures 
• Users must familiarize themselves with the locations of fire extinguishers, first aid 
kits, eyewash stations, and emergency exits. 
• In case of fire or serious injury, call emergency services and notify staff 
immediately. 
• All accidents or injuries must be reported to staff, regardless of severity. 
6. Responsibility and Enforcement 
• Users are responsible for their own safety and the safety of others in the 
Makerspace. 
• Failure to comply with safety rules may result in disciplinary action. 
7. Personal Project & Student Organization Usage 
• All users wishing to utilize the facility outside of required coursework or 
employment must sign and complete both the Photograph Release and 
Indemnity and Release of Liability, Indemnification and Assumption of the Risk 
Agreement (Adults / Minors). There are no exceptions. 
• For student organization usage, students should coordinate with their budget 
manager or faculty advisor regarding accounting information. 
• For any non-academic personal use of the facility, account information must be 
on file. Failure to settle outstanding balances may result in academic holds, 
preventing registration or the release of diplomas until all outstanding balances 
are settled. 
• Students wishing to use Ingram Hall Makerspace for personal projects may 
qualify for internal rates when sponsored by a faculty member who agrees to 
serve as a project and budgeting mentor. 
• Students wishing to use Ingram Hall Makerspace for personal projects who 
decline to use a faculty project mentor will classify as external users in 
accordance with R/PPS No. 3.06. 
• A 3% processing fee will be applied to all invoices settled via credit card.

title: Policies and Procedures IGRM 1202D
text:
Last Updated: February 2026 
Ingram Hall Makerspace – Project Work Room (IGRM 1202D) 
1. General Rules 
• Access is limited to TXST students, staff, faculty, or authorized guests. 
Unauthorized visitors are not allowed into any room of the Makerspace. 
2. Booking & Access 
• Access to the room itself requires no reservations, though certain equipment, 
worktables, and other similar items may require reservations. 
• Card access may be granted through FOM and the completion of prerequisite 
room/equipment access and training quizzes. 
3. Room Arrangement & Policies 
• IGRM 1202D has several project tables designated for project use for short-
periods. When entering the room, these are located on the right side of the room. 
• The left side of the room is designated for classroom instructional use and its 
associated equipment. General loitering, assembly, equipment use or any similar 
activity should not occur on this side of the room without permission from the 
supervising Mechanical Engineering Faculty. 
• Kardex Vertical Lift Module (VLM) trays are available for monthly rental. These 
can be rented via the FOM “Lending Items” Menu. 
• The Kardex should only be operated by those with active tray reservations. Any 
items in trays that are not under a rental agreement will be discarded. 
• Instructions for operation of the VLM are posted on the machine. For more 
assistance, please find an MST. 
• Users must be respectful of shared spaces and maintain a clean and organized 
work area. 
• Any projects, materials, or equipment left in the room (excluding on tables with 
an active reservation or in a VLM tray) may be discarded. No items should be left 
on the floor at any time. The Makerspace is not responsible for any loss or 
damage resulting from these actions. 
• All tools, equipment, and materials must be returned to their designated locations 
after use.

title: SOP FFF Feb26
text: Policy Reminders•Reserving a 3D Printer in FOM is not only required, it is impossible to print anything without doing so•The following trainings are required for using the Prusa CoreOne or Prusa Mini printers•Fused Filament Fabrication Policy and Procedures Quiz (FOM)•LinkedIn Learning FFF Certificate•In addition to the above trainings, the following trainings are also required for using the PrusaXL printers:•Multi-Material FFF Policy and Procedures Quiz (FOM)Revision 1.0 (Spring 2026) 2

title: SOP FFF Feb26
text: Policy Reminder (cont.)•Unless a printer is labeled “BYOF” the only allowable filament is PLA supplied by the Makerspace•Printers labeled “BYOF” may not use any Makerspace filament and the user supplies their own•Any filament is allowed, provided it matches the capabilities of the printer•Ask a Makerspace staff member for questions regarding material compatibility•There is a 30-minute minimum charge for all 3D Printer usage•Users are permitted to check out multiple printers simultaneously, with no set maximum limit.•Avoid touching moving parts while printing•Be careful of the printer's hot endRevision 1.0 (Spring 2026) 3

title: SOP FFF Feb26
text: Using Orca Slicer•Orca Slicer is the recommended slicing program for all Prusa printers managed by the Makerspace•Printers and profiles are pre-configured on Makerspace computers•When using orca slicer make sure all your printer requirements are correct.•Specifically, ensure the correct printer and filament type are selected•To start first open the application. The icon should look like this:Revision 1.0 (Spring 2026) 5

text: Importing files to Orca•To import files to Orca click the "add" icon at the top. It should look like a cube.•Once clicked, select your file (.stl or .3mf) and upload.•Your selected file should now appear on the build plate.Revision 1.0 (Spring 2026) 7

title: SOP FFF Feb26
text:
Using Orca Slicer•You can now prepare your print•On the lefthand side of the prepare page are all your printer settings.•Ensure the correct printer is selected•Prusa CoreOne = Prusa CORE One HF 0.4 nozzle•Prusa Mini = Prusa MINIIS 0.4 nozzle•In general, most prints will be successful by selecting "PawPrint Studio Default"Revision 1.0 (Spring 2026) 8

title: SOP FFF Feb26
text: Print orientation•Once your object is imported it might be in the wrong orientation and will be unable to print properly.•You will typically receive an error regarding hanging regions•Ensure that you click either "Auto orient" or "lay on face" to properly orient your object.•Your object should now be in the correct orientation to print.Revision 1.0 (Spring 2026) 9

title: SOP FFF Feb26
text: Slicing an object•Ensure that the appropriate printer is selected•Prusa CoreOne•Prusa Mini•Prusa XL (requires additional training)•Ensure that the correct slicer settings are applied (profile)•Ensure that the correct material is selected (PLA)•Then to slice an object, click the "Slice Plate" button•You should now have a sliced object ready for export Revision 1.0 (Spring 2026) 10
